tool.name: PyEuk cluster (current)
tool.description: wIBS distance, cluster sweep, and graphical HTML report
tool.command: mkdir -p wrk && export TMPDIR="\$(pwd)/wrk" && python '$__tool_directory__/pyeuk_cluster.py' --sheet '$sheet' --matrix-out '$distance_matrix' --clusters-out '$clusters' --sweep-out '$sweep' --report-out '$report' --n-boot $advanced.n_boot --linkage-method $advanced.linkage_method --report-flavor $advanced.report_flavor --report-theme $advanced.report_theme --min-completeness $advanced.min_completeness --k-min $advanced.k_min --k-max $advanced.k_max --report-excluded $advanced.report_excluded --project-psd $advanced.project_psd --cut $advanced.cut #if str($advanced.linkage_threshold).strip() != '' --linkage-threshold $advanced.linkage_threshold #end if

param.label: Minimum locus completeness
param.help: Minimum fraction of loci a specimen must have called to enter the matrix.

param.label: Project distances onto the PSD cone
param.help: Project the distance matrix onto the PSD cone. Off by default; leave off with count, turn on with distance.

param.label: How to cut the tree
param.help: How to cut the tree. count for a closed investigation; distance for surveillance, where unrelated specimens stay as singletons.

param.label: Distance to cut at
param.help: Dissimilarity to cut at in distance mode. Leave empty to calibrate from the data.

param.label: Report excluded specimens
param.help: List specimens excluded on completeness as cluster -1.

param.label: Bootstrap resamples (sweep confidence)
param.help: Bootstrap resamples for branch support in the sweep.

param.label: Linkage method
param.help: Linkage for the tree. ward by default; single follows transmission chains.

param.label: Report theme
param.help: Report theme. galaxy uses no external assets; studio links Google Fonts.

tool.help:
Runs the distance and the clustering in one step: it takes a haplotype sheet and returns the pairwise wIBS distance matrix, a cluster assignment, a stability sweep, and an HTML report.
**Distance.** Pairwise heterozygosity-weighted identity-by-state, computed over the windows called in both specimens, weighting each haplotype by its expected heterozygosity ``2p(1-p)`` and dividing by locus ploidy. See the standalone PyEuk distance tool for the full definition.
**Clustering.** Agglomerative hierarchical clustering under Ward's minimum-variance criterion, then one of two modes:
* **count** -- selects a cluster number k from the largest merge-height gap, subject to a relative gap of at least 0.22 and a minimum cluster size of ``max(2, min(5, floor(0.10 n)))``. Specimens in sub-threshold clusters stay unassigned. For a closed investigation where every accepted specimen belongs to a group and pairs of two are uninformative. * **distance** -- cuts the tree at an absolute dissimilarity without choosing k, leaving unrelated specimens as singletons. For surveillance, where forcing singletons into a low k invents linkage. Without labels the cut is the 5th percentile of pairwise distances; with labelled pairs it is ``median + 3 x 1.4826 x MAD`` of the within-cluster distances.
**Sweep.** Partition stability is assessed by subsampling 85% of specimens without replacement over 200 resamples and accumulating pairwise co-assignment. A pair is decisively resolved when ``|2p - 1| >= 0.5``; stable cores are connected components of pairs co-assigned at least 90% of the time. Candidate k are judged by the merge-height gap knee, silhouette width, and the gap statistic; when they agree the partition is reported as determined, otherwise a stability range ``[k_min, k_max]`` is reported instead of a forced point estimate.
Choose the mode from study design, not organism: the two are not interchangeable, and no label-free test reliably tells an outbreak cohort from a surveillance one. @HELP_FOOTER@
